title: Lula’s Comeback, European Energy Woes, Israeli Election Tensions, and the AI IPO Test
summary: This briefing covers Brazil’s historic election victory for Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and its implications for democracy, environment, and markets; soaring European gas prices amid Middle East tensions affecting energy security and costs; ongoing social unrest in France with government responses to rising living costs; Israel’s tense election with expatriates flying home to vote and its geopolitical significance; and the highly anticipated IPO of AI firm Anthropic, testing the financial viability of the AI boom. These stories highlight critical political, economic, and technological trends impacting premium beverages, FMCG, and hospitality sectors in France and internationally.

sources.title: Leaders across Americas react to Brazil President Lula's re-election
sources.summary: ​President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won Brazil's presidential election on Sunday (October 25), defeating right-wing ​Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in a runoff to secure a fourth non-consecutive term.

sources.title: 'Lula accustomed to negotiating tough bargains': Campaign promises collide with right-wing Congress
sources.summary: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Christopher Sabatini, Director of Chatham House's Latin America Programme. Sabatini examines how Lula's campaign reinvention, youth mobilisation, and the changing dynamics of Bolsonarismo are reshaping Brazil's political landscape. By embracing social media, mobilising younger voters, and shifting attention from his historical achievements to the economic anxieties of ordinary Brazilians, Lula managed to transform the electoral contest. As Sabatini explains, voters were no longer satisfied with hearing about the past. They wanted an answer to a more immediate question: "What are you going to do for us now?

sources.title: Lula wins fourth term in dramatic Brazil election comeback
sources.summary: The left-wing incumbent president had lost the first round to right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro.

sources.title: Lula's re-election brings hope for the Amazon as deforestation drops to record low
sources.summary: Climate activists in Brazil and beyond are celebrating President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's election victory as good news for the Amazon rainforest. His last four years in power saw a record decrease in deforestation in the world's largest rainforest, appropriately nicknamed the planet's lungs. FRANCE 24's Environment Editor Valerie Dekimpe tells us more.

sources.title: ‘Democracy always’: Lula vows no return to dictatorship in Brazil after election win
sources.summary: Leaders and governments worldwide congratulate Lula on dramatic comeback seen as an important signal to rest of Latin America Lula supporters celebrate election victory – in pictures Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva , the Brazilian president, has vowed that dictatorship and fascism will never return to Brazil after winning a historic fourth term in power by defeating his far-right opponent, Flávio Bolsonaro. “This is God’s work – and it’s thanks to all of you,” Lula told tens of thousands of supporters who had gathered in central São Paulo in the early hours of Monday to celebrate his dramatic election comeback. Continue reading...

sources.title: European gas prices soar to four-year high over winter supply fears
sources.summary: Jump fuelled by fears of further Middle East supply disruptions amid reports of US-Israeli plans to strike Iran European gas prices have jumped to levels not seen since 2022 as fears continue to grow around the continent’s supply this winter and the conflict in the Middle East. Wholesale gas prices hit €97 (£81) a megawatt-hour on Monday, as temperatures across Europe fell and traders priced in stronger demand for heating. Continue reading...

sources.title: France protests: Macron rules out state of emergency – for now
sources.summary: The French government sought to draw a line Monday under weeks of protests that have been marred by violence, with President Emmanuel Macron heading to Marseille. France has been rocked by widespread anger over the rising cost of living, with nationwide demonstrations on October 17 degenerating into some of the country's worst rioting in years.

sources.title: Macron promises 'concrete measures' in response to French students' demands
sources.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron said the government would announce “concrete measures" on Monday (October 26) to address school students’ demands after weeks of unrest. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu was scheduled to meet with students later Monday. FRANCE 24's Luke Shrago reports from the ground.

sources.title: Tens of thousands of Israelis living abroad expected to fly in for pivotal vote
sources.summary: Israelis are preparing to head to the polls on Tuesday (October 27). Unable to vote from abroad, tens of thousands of expatriate citizens have been flying in from across the world to cast their ballots. FRANCE 24's Noga Tarnopolsky met some of them at the airport.

sources.title: Opponents accuse Netanyahu of stoking tensions with Iran before Israel's election
sources.summary: Israel's defence minister denied on Monday (October 26) reports of a rift between PM Netanyahu and the army over Iran, before the vote. Netanyahu has campaigned heavily on his security credentials, insisting only he can "finish the job" in the US-Israeli war on Iran. His main rival, ex-army chief Gadi Eisenkot, has accused him of playing up the Iran threat when it suits him politically, and of failing to accomplish his war goals. FRANCE 24's Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.

sources.title: Israeli candidate Eisenkot pledges to unite country as Netanyahu deems him 'soft' on Iran
sources.summary: Israeli presidential candidate Gadi Eisenkot's pledge made Sunday to "heal" Israeli society after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's divisive tenure resonated with some voters attending his final campaign rally before polling begins Tuesday. Netanyahu meanwhile received fresh backing for re-election from US President Donald Trump and deemed Eisenkot "soft" on Iran.

sources.title: Israel election: unable to vote from abroad, expats have to fly home
sources.summary: Israelis can’t vote from abroad, so tens of thousands of expats are expected to fly home for the election. At Tel Aviv airport, supporters of opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot are already waiting at arrivals. A “Fly and Vote” initiative helps expats organise their trip, despite a failed petition from Netanyahu’s Likud party to restrict it. With polls predicting a tight race, every vote could count, and the result will decide the Prime Minister’s fate.

sources.title: Anthropic warns of 'catastrophic risk' to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing
sources.summary: The company will be the first true artificial intelligence company to go public as tech firms continue to invest heavily in AI.

sources.title: Anthropic IPO filing reveals rapid revenue gains and even larger losses
sources.summary: Market debut of AI company behind Claude chatbot will be one of largest in US history, a test of the AI boom’s financial viability Anthropic has publicly filed for a stock market listing in what is slated to be one of the largest debuts in history. The company’s float on the US market will serve as a test of the financial viability of the multitrillion-dollar AI boom. Analysts and investors have valued the San Francisco-based company, founded in 2021, at more than $1.5tn. The company, which will will list under the symbol ANT, confidentially filed with US financial regulators for an initial public offering in June. Continue reading...
